subject: Final wire routing for invoice + intermediary fee & tax handling (SG cover options)
messages:
From: Globex Accounts Payable <accounts-payable@globex.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@globex.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Payment for INV-7789 — wire instructions?

Marcus,

We’ve received invoice INV-7789 for Redwood’s June usage charge. Our payment team is ready to wire but needs final wiring instructions and confirmation of what currency the invoice should be paid in (USD vs EUR), and whether we should use our Singapore correspondent bank or route via our US bank.

A couple of specific questions from our treasury team:
- If we route via our Singapore correspondent (DBSSGSG), will any intermediary bank fees be deducted from the beneficiary amount or will you accept cover payments (sender pays all)?
- The invoice lists Redwood Europe BV as the billed entity — does Redwood want this paid net of GST/VAT or gross? We’re in APAC and our system may need a tax code.

Attached: INV-7789-Redwood-2028-06.pdf

Thanks,
Diego Alvarez
Accounts Payable — Globex Corp.
[Attachment: INV-7789-Redwood-2028-06.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Globex Accounts Payable <accounts-payable@globex.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Payment for INV-7789 — wire instructions?

Diego — thanks for the quick note and the invoice. Short answers up front: we can accept payment either to our US operating account (USD) or to Redwood Europe BV (EUR). For this specific invoice we prefer EUR to match the billed entity, but we can accept USD if it’s simpler for your treasury.

Important routing and fee options:
- Preferred (clean beneficiary credit): Instruct your bank to send an outright beneficiary-credit wire to our Barclays London account (EUR). If you route via DBSSGSG (Singapore), intermediary bank fees are common; we normally ask for sender-cover so the full invoice amount posts to Redwood.
- Alternative (sender cannot cover): If your bank will not cover intermediaries, please instruct CHARGES: SHA and we will absorb up to USD 15 of intermediary fees for this single invoice as a one-off concession. Anything above that would be netted from the received amount.

Wire details (EUR — Redwood Europe BV):
- Beneficiary: Redwood Europe BV
- IBAN: GB29BARC2041XXXXXXX (example)
- BIC/SWIFT: BARCGB22XXX
- Bank name: Barclays Bank PLC, London
- Reference: INV-7789 / Globex Corp

If you choose USD to Redwood US LLC, let me know and I’ll provide the USD nostro and preferred cover instruction.

Tax: because the invoice bills Redwood Europe BV and references a B2B service, we expect VAT reverse-charge to apply for EU VAT treatment. However, for your APAC ledger we can provide the invoice with a zero-rated VAT line and the EUR gross amount; please confirm what tax code your AP team needs.

I’ll loop finance internally to confirm the one-time fee concession and to make sure the NetSuite invoice (INV-7789) is tagged correctly for VAT.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-bank-rails.csv (CSV)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 12:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Payment for INV-7789 — confirm concession and tax coding

Marcus / Marissa — forwarding. We’re OK to absorb up to USD 15 of intermediary fees for this single one-off (take from COGS/discretionary). Please confirm accounting tag and whether we should switch the invoice to Redwood US LLC if Globex prefers USD routing.

Neha — need VAT reverse-charge confirmation. Globex is a non-EU payer routing from SG — do we need any additional documentation on the AP side to support reverse-charge (e.g., their VAT ID / EORI)? If not, mark as zero-rated service and note the customer location in the invoice metadata.

Laura Bennett
Finance Manager — Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 08:21:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Payment for INV-7789 — confirm concession and tax coding

Laura / Marcus — quick tax note: since the billed legal entity is Redwood Europe BV, and this is a B2B supply of services, the invoice should carry the reverse charge note and include the customer VAT ID if they have one. If Globex cannot provide a VAT ID (many APAC purchasers do not have EU VAT IDs), we should still document their country of registration and apply zero-rated export if the service qualifies — but that’s riskier from an audit POV.

Action: ask Globex for their APAC VAT/GST registration or at minimum a company registration number and billing address. If they cannot provide, switch billing to Redwood US LLC and accept USD wire (fewer VAT complications).

Neha Kapoor
Tax Lead — Redwood Inference

Diego / AP team — thanks for bearing with us. Final guidance below based on how you want to route: 

Option A — You want to pay EUR to Redwood Europe BV (preferred):
- Instruct beneficiary-credit wire to Barclays London as below (same as prior):
  - Beneficiary: Redwood Europe BV
  - IBAN: GB29BARC2041XXXXXXX
  - BIC: BARCGB22XXX
  - Charges: Please send as OUR (sender pays intermediaries) if possible. If your bank can only do SHA, please let us know and we will absorb up to USD 15 in intermediary deductions for this invoice only (Redwood concession).
- Tax: Please provide Globex VAT/GST registration number if available. If you can’t provide an EU VAT ID, inform us and we will either re-issue the invoice as Redwood US LLC in USD or leave as Redwood Europe BV but annotate the invoice with your billing country and registration number for our records.

Option B — You prefer to pay USD to Redwood US LLC (faster for your treasury):
- Beneficiary: Redwood US LLC
- Bank: Wells Fargo NA (example)
- Account: 123456789
- Routing: FWBLUS6SXXX (Swift) / ABA 121000248 (US domestic)
- Charges: SHA is fine; we’ll accept net and mark for USD posting. No VAT on the US bill.

Please confirm which option you’ll use and attach the payment confirmation once the wire is initiated. We’ll close the invoice in NetSuite when payment posts.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
